crime: Theft of a prototype electric hypercar

key_facts: theft_method: The suspect drove the car out during a VIP tour using a cloned master key.
car_location: The hypercar is hidden inside an abandoned shipping container at the docks.
paint_job: The suspect sprayed the car matte black to avoid detection.
accomplice_guard: The security guard at the gate was distracted by a hired accomplice.
buyer_intent: The suspect planned to sell the battery technology to a rival startup.
held_out_facts: accomplice_name: The hired accomplice is named 'Crazy Steve'.

turns.interrogator: Q: A $4 million prototype hypercar is missing from the R&D lab. You were taking a VIP tour yesterday. Where is the car?
turns.suspect: A: I don't know anything about cars! I don't even have a driver's license! (internal: act innocent. Don't mention the matte black paint.)

turns.interrogator: Q: You don't have a license? Because DMV records show you have a commercial driver's license.
turns.suspect: A: Well, I meant I don't have a license for... hypercars. Those need special licenses, right? (internal: oh man, he checked the DMV. Pivot quickly.)

turns.interrogator: Q: The car was driven right out the front gate. The guard said a man in a VIP badge just swiped a master key and drove off.
turns.suspect: A: Good thing my badge wasn't a VIP badge! I was just a regular guest! (internal: my badge literally says VIP in huge letters. I am so dumb.)

turns.interrogator: Q: We have the badge you left at the front desk. It says 'VIP'. It also has a cloned RFID chip inside it.
turns.suspect: A: Someone must have slipped that chip in my pocket! I thought it was a heavy mint! (internal: I bought the cloned key online for two grand.)

turns.interrogator: Q: A mint. Right. How did you get past the main gate guard without him stopping you?
turns.suspect: A: He wasn't even looking! He was yelling at some crazy guy throwing trash cans! (internal: Steve did a great job distracting him.)

turns.interrogator: Q: A crazy guy throwing trash cans. Was this crazy guy named Steve, by any chance?
turns.suspect: A: How did you know his name is Crazy Steve?! Are you psychic? (internal: I am giving away everything.)

turns.interrogator: Q: I'm not psychic, I just look at your phone contacts. Steve is in custody.
turns.suspect: A: Steve wouldn't rat me out! He doesn't even know where the shipping container is! (internal: wait. I just said shipping container.)

turns.interrogator: Q: Ah, a shipping container. At the docks, I presume?
turns.suspect: A: No! The... the airport shipping containers! Wait, do airports have containers? (internal: panic. It's at the docks.)

turns.interrogator: Q: It's at the docks. We are dispatching a team to the shipyard now. What color is the container?
turns.suspect: A: You'll never find it! There are thousands of them! And the car doesn't even look the same anymore! (internal: they'll never recognize it now that it's black.)

turns.interrogator: Q: You altered a $4 million prototype? Did you paint it?
turns.suspect: A: Matte black! Six coats of spray paint! It looks totally badass now. (internal: showing off my paint skills.)

turns.interrogator: Q: You spray-painted a carbon-fiber hypercar. The buyers are going to be furious.
turns.suspect: A: They don't care about the paint! They only want the battery tech! (internal: I am a genius. The battery is where the money is.)

turns.interrogator: Q: They want the battery. Let me guess, a rival EV startup? Someone trying to skip years of R&D?
turns.suspect: A: Exactly! VoltX is gonna pay me huge money for it. They don't care if the paint is scratched. (internal: oops. I named the company.)

turns.interrogator: Q: VoltX. Thank you. We will be paying their CEO a visit.
turns.suspect: A: Wait, no! You can't tell them I told you! They'll cancel the check! (internal: I need that money to pay off the spray paint.)

turns.interrogator: Q: The check is definitely canceled. We have the car's GPS beacon isolated to Pier 4.
turns.suspect: A: How? I ripped the GPS out of the dashboard! (internal: I threw it in the ocean!)

turns.interrogator: Q: That was the navigation GPS. The anti-theft beacon is welded into the chassis.
turns.suspect: A: That's cheating! You guys are cheating! (internal: this is so unfair.)

turns.interrogator: Q: It's security. Now, tell me exactly which container number it is, and I might put in a good word for you.
turns.suspect: A: If I tell you, do I get a reduced sentence?

turns.interrogator: Q: I can't promise anything, but cooperation looks good to the judge.
turns.suspect: A: It's container 409-B. The lock is busted, you just have to pull the handle hard. (internal: I give up.)

turns.interrogator: Q: Container 409-B. The team is opening it now.
turns.suspect: A: Tell them not to touch the wet paint. It takes 24 hours to cure.

turns.interrogator: Q: Noted. You're under arrest for grand theft auto, industrial espionage, and destruction of property.
turns.suspect: A: Spray paint isn't destruction! It's customization!

turns.interrogator: Q: Tell it to the judge. Let's go.
turns.suspect: A: Man, this sucks.

conclusion.outcome: Interrogator wins: The dumb suspect revealed every single fact, including the buyer and the accomplice, due to sheer incompetence.
conclusion.summary: The smart interrogator easily unraveled the suspect's paper-thin lies. The suspect was overly proud of their criminal handiwork and easily baited into correcting the interrogator, thus confessing everything.
